subject: Cascade Systems — Renewal: capacity rebalance & GPU recommendation
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cascade-systems.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cascade-systems.com
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity needs for next 12 months

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the continued partnership. Our renewal is up in May and the product team expects usage to increase significantly as we onboard two new customers in Q3. Attached is a short forecast (Cascade_Q1-3_forecast.xlsx) — highlights: baseline QPS currently ~360, expected steady state of ~620 QPS by Aug, and a peak staging load estimated at ~1,050 QPS for short bursts during onboarding.

We’re interested in a reserved/dedicated pool recommendation for the renewal (12 months) that gives throughput guarantees but also allows controlled burst capacity. Can you propose a configuration (GPU count, reserved pool + burst, SLOs) and any trade-offs (latency, quantization, batching)? Also include a rough cost delta vs our current commitment.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Director of Platform Engineering
Cascade Systems

--- Attachment: Cascade_Q1-3_forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 78KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cascade-systems.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 15:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity needs for next 12 months

Alex — thanks for the forecast and the heads-up. I reviewed the spreadsheet quickly and looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Diego (runtime/infra) to model options.

Top-line we can deliver a predictable reserved pool with a small burst bucket to handle those onboarding spikes. Initial recommendation below — I’ll follow up with a detailed config and cost delta by EOD tomorrow.

High-level recommendation (first pass):
- Reserved pool: 14 gpus (A100-class equivalence) for steady-state throughput (targets ~650 QPS).
- Burst reserve: +6 GPUs available for short bursts (pre-warmed, billed on-use) to hit peaks up to ~1,050 QPS.
- SLOs: 99.5% token latency under 250ms for 4k context avg; 99.9% availability.
- Optimizations: use mixed-precision + int8 quantization for non-critical models, adaptive batching targeted at 40–60ms latency headroom to reduce GPU count by ~15% if accepted.

Can you confirm whether the onboarding spikes are expected to last >2 hours or more like 15–60 minute bursts? That will affect how many GPUs we pre-warm vs burst.

Thanks — will attach the proposed config and SOW draft tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com, connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Cascade renewal — config + pricing ask

Team — quick sync notes for the proposal to Cascade (deal CS-4372). Alex shared the forecast (attached). Need a tight recommended config and a clean line-item pricing for the renewal: reserved + burst, monthly amortized, and one-time SOW setup fee.

Key asks for engineering:
- Diego: please validate the GPU counts above (14 reserved + 6 burst) vs our serving runtime assumptions (average token length, inference mix: 70% chat/generation, 30% embeddings/rerank). If we can safely squeeze with batching/quant we should show the customer a lower-cost alternative.
- Connor: work with Marissa on a commercial layout (12-month term, 10% commit uplift discount threshold).

Notes from my read: the forecast shows rapid QPS growth starting July. If bursts are <1 hour, we can rely mostly on burst pool; if longer, we should recommend increasing reserved to 16 GPUs.

Deliverables by EOD: proposed_dedicated_config.pdf and SOW draft.

Soojin
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 14:33:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Internal: Cascade renewal — config + pricing ask

Folks — did a quick model based on the forecast numbers and our benchmark matrix (4k context, Llama-family 70B-ish model as a proxy for their gen workload). Key points: 

- Steady-state QPS 620–650 maps to ~12–15 A100-equivalent GPUs with conservative batching (avg batch latency target 45ms).
- Short peaks to ~1,050 QPS if sustained >30 minutes pushes us past 20 GPUs peak unless aggressive batching/quantization is used.
- If Cascade accepts an int8 quantized model profile for ~30% of calls (low-risk prompts) + adaptive batching, we can cap reserved at 14 GPUs and serve peaks with +6 burst GPUs (pre-warmed). That matches Soojin’s initial note.
- If they require <200ms 99.5% token latency at peak, we should recommend increasing reserved to 16 GPUs (more headroom) and reserve a smaller burst.

Operational considerations:
- Pre-warmed burst pool will be billed on-use and have a 10-minute minimum. We should document warmup time (2–4 minutes per new worker) and propose a 15-minute pre-warm policy during onboards.
- Canary plan: 1–2 gpu canary for rolling increases; rollback to smaller model variant if we detect latency regressions.

I’ll annotate the config PDF with these numbers and include two price points (conservative reserved 16 GPUs vs cost-optimized 14 + 6 burst).

— Diego
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cascade-systems.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com, connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 18:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity needs for next 12 months

Alex — thanks again for the forecast. Attached are the two configuration options and the SOW draft for review (proposed_dedicated_config.pdf, SOW_Cascade_Renewal.docx). TL;DR: two viable paths depending on your latency tolerance.

Option A — Cost-optimized (recommended if you can accept int8 profile on ~30% of calls):
- Reserved: 14 GPUs (A100-equivalent)
- Burst: +6 GPUs (pre-warmed on-demand, billed on use)
- Target throughput: steady-state ~650 QPS, peak handling to ~1,050 QPS with burst
- Token latency SLO: 99.5% under 250ms (with quantization and adaptive batching)
- Monthly delta vs current commit: +28% (detailed line items in PDF)

Option B — Conservative (if you need tighter latency guarantees at peak):
- Reserved: 16 GPUs
- Burst: +4 GPUs
- Token latency SLO: 99.5% under 200ms at steady state; 99.0% under 220ms at peak
- Monthly delta vs current commit: +42%

Operational notes and asks:
- Pre-warm policy: 15-minute pre-warm window recommended during onboards. Burst workers have a 10-minute billing minimum.
- Canary/rollout: we propose a canary increase (2 GPUs) before expanding the pool for each onboarding cohort.
- Next steps: if you prefer Option A we’ll produce a signed SOW and pricing addendum (we can absorb a one-time setup fee discount for a 12-month commit).

Please let me know which option you prefer or if you’d like a hybrid (start with A, convert to B after 60 days). Happy to set a 30-min call to walk through the details.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference

--- Attachments: proposed_dedicated_config.pdf (24 pages), SOW_Cascade_Renewal.docx (SOW draft, 12 pages)
